# VMDK external descriptors and selected companion files

The read-only importer now accepts base `monolithicFlat`, `twoGbMaxExtentFlat` and `twoGbMaxExtentSparse` descriptors. Existing standalone sparse/stream support is unchanged. The user first selects the descriptor, then explicitly selects its missing companions in a separate multiple-file picker. Partial selections can be completed in later selections. Nothing resolves paths, searches directories, opens devices or follows parents. Only bytes, logical geometry and the primary basename cross existing native inspection IPC.

Descriptors require version 1, a valid CID, `parentCID=ffffffff`, 512-byte logical sectors and homogeneous FLAT/SPARSE extents matching createType. RW and RDONLY are read identically. FLAT requires an explicit sector offset. Sparse capacity must match its extent; compressed split extents and nonempty embedded descriptors are rejected. QEMU's reserved zero-filled descriptor region is supported and rechecked. Extent names must be ordinary basenames; device names, paths, alternate streams, ambiguous case/Unicode-normalized names, duplicate sparse references and overlapping shared flat ranges are rejected. Nonoverlapping ranges in one selected flat file are supported. No full-content identity is available: matching names and geometry cannot prove the selected files belong together; details explain this.

Bounds: 64 extents/64 selected companions, 64 KiB descriptor, 4 MiB–8 TiB combined logical disk; individual sparse tails may be as small as 512 bytes. Sparse mapping, captured metadata and physical-read budgets are shared across all parts (32 MiB map, 66 MiB metadata, 160 MiB reads/100000 calls). Combined logical reads are limited to 1 MiB/request and 4 MiB total. Descriptors, sparse indexes/empty descriptor areas and accessed flat bytes are re-read before accepting inspection. This is not an immutable snapshot or a complete content check. Unreferenced files are never read. File-count and file-size details count only distinct used files plus the descriptor.

## Independent synthetic fixtures

`scripts/create-vmdk-bundle-fixtures.mjs` exclusively creates a new `.vm/vmdk-bundle-fixtures` directory; it refuses an existing output directory. Input is the existing synthetic 8 MiB `vmdk-raw.gz`, not a user disk. QEMU 10.2 creates monolithic flat and split sparse containers. To exercise actual cross-file boundaries without a >2 GiB fixture, two independently converted 4 MiB sparse extents are combined in an explicit descriptor. Two flat extents include nonzero 512-byte prefixes, testing declared offsets. QEMU only accepts RW extent syntax, so the RDONLY flat application fixture has an otherwise identical RW oracle descriptor.

All four QEMU oracle descriptors passed `qemu-img check` and complete logical `compare` against RAW. Outputs are recorded in `.vm/vmdk-bundle-fixtures.log`; small gzip regression copies are named `vmdk-bundle-*.gz`. This is QEMU/synthetic compatibility evidence, not VMware-created corpus coverage or VM device acceptance. No running VM, mount or raw device was used.

Nine reader regression tests cover exact head/tail/EBR and cross-file bytes, offsets, missing/unused files, matching/ambiguity, dependencies and syntax, shared-file overlap, truncation/change detection, sparse geometry, tiny tails and shared resource limits. Two additional backend tests verify missing-file errors before IPC and exact combined bytes through byte-only native inspection.

Still excluded: snapshot/differencing chains, VMFS/SEsparse/RDM/ZERO extents, encryption, 4Kn VMDK, content browsing/export, creation/conversion/mounting, and compatibility with a broader VMware corpus. Support here means partition-table display/checks only.

Format reference: [QEMU VMDK implementation](https://github.com/qemu/qemu/blob/master/block/vmdk.c), including external descriptor extent parsing, header creation and split-file generation. Final build/UI/check results are recorded separately in `.vm/vmdk-bundle-status.json`.
